summary: Ryusei Keira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Lausanne by 2003 under the supervision of Tom Tillemans.
Ryushin Kitao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Shuchiin University, attested in 2014 and 2026.
Ryushin Saito specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a professorship at Bukkyo University (attested 2015) and served on the faculty at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Ryushin Sudo (1929–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho University from around 1948 to 1952. He later served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Ryukoku University around 1951 to 1959. He was affiliated with the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute in 1962 and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University from around 1968 to 1998.

Ryusho Hikata (1892–1991) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held posts at Kyushu University, Fukuoka Women's University, and the Japan Academy.

Ryuta Kikutani works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts as an expert researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015), at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center (attested 2020), and as an associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Ryutaro Tsuchida studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, he was an assistant at Marburg (~1980–1983) before becoming a professor and later professor emeritus (1995–2012) at Tokyo.

Ryutoku Kimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1966–1970). He worked as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1979), a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).
Ryuyu Saito works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1916, he studied under Chishu Kitagawa and the traditional teacher Chijo Kitagawa.
Ryōmin Akizuki (1921–1999) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo around 1947–1950. He later held a post at Saitama Medical University.

Rüdiger Schmitt is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann around 1958 to 1965 and held a post at Saarland University from around 1972 to 2004.
S. A. S. Sarma is an Indologist who held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2004 and 2024.
S. Bhaskaran Nair worked in Indology, serving at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute as general editor (attested 1944 and 1992) and as deputy director (attested 1974–1977 and 1986).

S. D. Laddu (1926–2021) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He was affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1968) and served as editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).
S. Ghosh worked in Tibetology, serving as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as editor for the Bulletin of Tibetology, both attested in 1982.
S. K. Maity worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham from around 1950 to 1953 and held a post at Jadavpur University from around 1958 to 1986.

S. K. Ramanatha Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as junior lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras until 1938 and held a temporary post at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Madras. He taught at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909) and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929).
